Title: August 6, 2026 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting

Topic1.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic1.Summary: Residents spoke during open comment on topics including Palestine and Israel, the Fort Chambers interpretive design, Spruce Pool repairs, permanently affordable housing HOA costs, shelter sanitary conditions, and council investment divestment. Staff responded on open space, Spruce Pool closure through Labor Day, HOA affordability, and the shelter bathroom issue. Council members commented on tribal consultation and investment portfolio governance.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda and Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic2.Summary: Council passed the consent agenda items 3A through 3C. Three outside city utility permit requests for properties on Cherryville Road, Frying Pan Road, and Cottonwood Drive were reviewed during call-up check-ins and none were called up.

Topic3.Title: Ballot Measures Staff Presentation
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented five potential November 2026 ballot measures: the recreation and safety bond, the residential vacancy excise tax, the firefighter collective bargaining charter amendment, the debt limit charter amendment, and the downtown development authority. Staff explained financial pressures, the long-term financial strategy, facilities backlog of 15 priority buildings, and DDA mechanics including tax increment financing and governance.

Topic4.Title: Public Hearing on Ballot Measures Public Comment
Topic4.Summary: Dozens of residents spoke on the five ballot measures. Supporters of the DDA cited downtown vacancies and small business needs, while opponents cited diversion of dedicated open space and library funds and lack of citizen input. Many speakers, especially from South Boulder, demanded binding language protecting South Boulder Rec Center amenities, and firefighters and the Boulder Chamber urged referral. Others supported the residential vacancy tax.

Topic5.Title: Ordinance 8761 Firefighter Collective Bargaining Charter Amendment
Topic5.Summary: Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8761 to refer to the November 3, 2026 ballot a charter amendment guaranteeing full-time fire department employees the right to bargain collectively. The measure was negotiated with IAFF Local 900 leadership and city staff.

Topic6.Title: Ordinance 8758 Recreation and Safety Bond
Topic6.Summary: Council adopted Ordinance 8758 as amended to refer a general obligation bond for recreation, public safety, and capital projects to the November ballot. The amendment changed South Boulder Rec Center language to specify a lap pool, after debate about specificity and community engagement. Projects include South Boulder Rec Center replacement, North Boulder Rec Center renovation, West Senior Center, a public safety building, and fire station renovations.

Topic7.Title: Ordinance 8759 Residential Vacancy Excise Tax
Topic7.Summary: Council voted 7 to 1 to refer Ordinance 8759 to the November ballot, which would impose a vacancy excise tax of 4,000 per unit on homes occupied 183 days or less per year starting January 1, 2028, with CPI adjustment up to 7,000. Council member Spear voted no. Council discussed possible exemptions such as probate.

Topic8.Title: Ordinance 8762 Debt Limit Charter Amendment
Topic8.Summary: Council unanimously approved Ordinance 8762 to refer to the November ballot an amendment to the Boulder home rule charter changing the city's debt limit calculation from assessed value to actual value, bringing the city in line with other Colorado communities and state statute.

Topic9.Title: Ordinance 8763 Downtown Development Authority
Topic9.Summary: Council debated Ordinance 8763 to form a Boulder Downtown Development Authority and refer it to November ballot. Supporters emphasized revitalizing downtown and University Hill, vacancies, and sales tax decline. Opponents raised concerns about diverting dedicated open space and library funds, nonresident corporate voting, lack of library and county engagement, and climate and water risks. A motion to add a post-approval engagement process failed 4-4. The main motion failed 4-4. Council then gave staff direction to scope next steps for continued community engagement, which received six votes.

Topic10.Title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Update Conditions and Amendments
Topic10.Summary: Council considered remaining conditions and recommended amendments to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update from planning board, the Board of County Commissioners, and county planning commission. Items included removing the history section, municipal airport policy 79, future land use changes in planning area 2, housing diversity policy 82, rural lands definition, near-transit language, and fire-adapted communities policy 89. Council approved all three motion sets unanimously, accepting staff recommendations, and asked for a future resolution on the history section.
